correctness.rationale: For every labelled finite cycle of order n>=3, every set of at most three points qualifies, while six circularly ordered selected points expose a pair with two blocked vertices on each arc. For exactly four selected points the only obstruction is a cyclic gap longer than floor(n/2); for five it is a two-consecutive-gap sum longer than floor(n/2). Every antipodal tie is handled by the alternate shortest arc. Exact positive-composition inclusion-exclusion counts the possible gaps: events on nonadjacent indices cannot intersect and no triple intersection is possible; all terms B and I are explicitly derived. Each s-subset is represented n/s times, giving exactly the displayed parity formulas. Direct exhaustive shortest-path tests for 3<=n<=18 and independent gap-composition tests for 5<=n<=32 both matched, but the proof is unrestricted.

value.rationale: A recently motivated tolerance hierarchy has a complete exact graph-set enumeration in its first genuinely new tolerance case. The result gives two explicit nontrivial coefficient formulas for every order, geometric necessary-and-sufficient conditions for all maximum sets, correct antipodal boundaries, and a limiting density 1/16 for size-five samples; these cannot be deduced from the known extremal cardinality alone. It is a structurally meaningful infinite-family polynomial, not a routine rewriting of the scalar maximum.
